title: Negative coordinate-noise contraction for all exponents above one
statement: For every $q\in\mathbb R$ with $q>1$, there exists $c\in\mathbb R$ with $0<c\le1$, and with $c=2/5$ whenever $q=4$ or $q=4/3$, such that for every nonnegative integer $n$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive coordinate atom weights summing to $1$, every coordinate $i$, and every real-valued function $f$ on its outcome space, $\|N_{i,-c}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$. Here $\|h\|_{q,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^q)^{1/q}$ and $N_{i,-c}h=h-L_i h-cL_i h$, with $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product of probability spaces
coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: For every $q>1$ there exists $0<c\le1$, with $c=2/5$ when $q\in\{4,4/3\}$, such that every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ satisfies $\|N_{i,-c}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every coordinate $i$ and real function $f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
